input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new `min` parameter defaults to 1 second, so every existing `wait_exponential_jitter` caller that relies on sub-second waits now has them silently raised to 1 second.
- rationale: Trigger: code calls wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1, max=10) without passing min. Before this change, the first wait could be about 0.1 to 1.1 seconds. Now the return value is max(max(0, 1), min(result, 10)), so the wait is always at least 1 second. The mechanism is the default value of min=1, which applies the new clamp to all callers. The impact is silently longer waits and different timing for existing users who did not ask for a minimum, and tests that assert on wait durations can break. The title announces a min parameter but not a changed default for existing behavior.
critique: The finding names the same defect as the label: the new `min` parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0. Because of that default, sub-second exponential waits are clamped up to 1 second for callers who never passed `min`.
